podcast.title: A dream that changed

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: What did you want to be when you were a child? Guess: what did Sam dream of becoming?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is dreams and ambitions. Leyla, what did you want to be when you were a child?
[laugh] A pilot! Then a singer, then a vet. My ambition changed every year. What about you?
A footballer. I trained every day after school. I really wanted to play for Manchester United.
So what happened?
When I was sixteen, I broke my leg. It was a big setback. I couldn't play for a year, and after that I was never fast enough.
Oh no. That must have been hard.
It was. But my coach said something I still remember: "Aim high, but don't forget to enjoy the game."
That's good advice. My role model is my aunt Nigar. She always wanted to be a doctor, but she married young and had three children.
And she gave up?
Never! At thirty-eight she went back to university. She studied at night while the kids slept. Now she's a children's doctor.
Wow. That's real determination.
And perseverance. She failed one big exam twice. The third time, she passed with the best result in her group.
Amazing. Where did she find the motivation?
She told me, "Chase your dreams while you still can. I didn't want to be seventy and still wondering."
I love that. So, Leyla, what do you aspire to now?
One day I'd like to open a small café with books — a quiet place where people can read and practise English.
A SpeakLab café! I'd come every day.
And you? Do you have a goal now?
I'm running a half marathon in the spring. It's not Manchester United, but I want to go after something difficult again.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is one dream you still have — and what is your first small step?
Mine is to finish the race — without breaking my leg. See you next time!
Bye for now!
